title: Applied ML Eval & Onboarding Integrated Playbook
author: Marina K. Lee
body:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates Redwood's standards and operational procedures for the Applied-ML evaluation (eval) ecosystem: the eval harness, curated prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding guidance, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage. The document is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML, SRE, and Product QA teams who are responsible for introducing, validating, and maintaining model variants in serving environments (hosted, dedicated, private).

Goals:
- Provide a single, repeatable onboarding flow that reduces time-to-serve while protecting production quality SLOs.
- Standardize eval artifacts (harness config, prompt sets, metrics, thresholds) so regressions are detectable and actionable.
- Define ownership, roles, and escalation paths for regression triage.
- Ensure quantized model variants meet minimum quality and latency targets before they are permitted in routing policies.

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies to all model onboarding requests (open-source or vendor-supplied) intended for any Redwood serving surface (hosted / dedicated / private).
- Includes base model evaluation, prompt set curation, synthetic and human-in-the-loop evals, latency/throughput profiling, and quantization validation.
- Does not replace customer-specific compliance checks; those run separately via the Private deployment security checklist.

Quick links (common tasks):
1) Start new model onboarding: create issue in APM-Model-Onboard board with tag `onboard-request` and attach model card + weights URL.
2) Run standard harness: `rwd-eval run --suite standard-onboarding --model <id>` (CI job: eval-harness/onboard-standard).
3) Add prompt set: use prompt catalog template (see Prompt Sets section) and open PR against `eval-prompt-sets` repo.

Roles & Ownership:
- Model Onboarding Lead (Applied ML): overall owner of the onboarding run, responsible for results and triage.
- Eval Harness Maintainers (Infra/Applied ML): own the harness code, CI, and baseline dataset updates.
- Quality Leads (Product/Applied ML): validate human-eval results and approve guardrail thresholds.
- SRE (Serving Runtime): responsible for quantization performance validation and deployment readiness.

Standards and Artifact Definitions:
- Eval Harness Configuration (required fields):
  - model_id (string)
  - model_variant (string, e.g., fp32, int8-ggml, q4_0)
  - seed (int)
  - prompt_sets (list of prompt_set_ids)
  - metrics (list of metric_names: accuracy, exact_match, rougeL, sacrebleu, toxicity, latency_p50/95/99, cost_per_token)
  - tags (list)

- Prompt Set: a curated JSONL of examples with fields: id, input, expected_output (optional), eval_type (generation/classification/extraction), and quality_labels (gold/human-reviewed). Prompt sets must include at least:
  - 500 objective examples for quantitative metrics (if available)
  - 50 human-reviewed examples for qualitative checks (safety, hallucination)

- Guardrail Suite: a named collection of checks that includes safety filters (toxicity, PII redaction checks), factuality heuristics (KB-lookup rate, hallucination flags), and style/format validators. Each check must include pass/fail thresholds and remediation notes.

Onboarding Flow (Step-by-step):
1) Intake and Triage (1 business day)
   1.1) Submit onboard-request issue with model provenance, license, architecture, and suggested target variants (fp32, int8, q4_0, etc.).
   1.2) Onboarding Lead confirms legal/licensing compliance with Security & Legal. If restricted, mark confidentiality `restricted`.

2) Baseline Eval (2-3 business days)
   2.1) Run `standard-onboarding` harness which executes: prompt-sets: standard-benchmarks, safety-checks, latency profile with representative sequence lengths (64/512/2048).
   2.2) Collect metrics: task-level accuracy, safety failure rates, latency P50/P95/P99, and tokenization cost.
   2.3) Record results in the Model Onboarding dashboard (sheet + eval DB) and tag model status `baseline-complete`.

3) Quality Guardrail Validation (parallel with Baseline)
   3.1) Run guardrail suite. Any check with severity `blocker` must be remediated before quantization or routing.
   3.2) For subjective checks, run a human evaluation with at least 30 raters across 50 seeded examples. Use majority vote and collect comments.

4) Quantization Experimentation (3-5 business days)
   4.1) SRE + Applied ML produce quantized variants per standard profiles (see Quantization Profiles below).
   4.2) Run `quant-eval` harness which runs both the full prompt set and an adversarial prompt subset.
   4.3) Acceptance criteria:
      - Relative metric drop <= 3% absolute for high-sensitivity tasks (classification/QA) or <= 5% for open generation fallback tasks.
      - Safety failure delta <= 0.5 percentage points.
      - Latency improvement >= 15% OR cost improvement >= 20% (to justify variant promotion).

5) Canary & Rollout (1-2 weeks)
   5.1) Promote accepted variant to canary (traffic <= 5%) with active monitoring on: error rate, latency P95, guardrail violations, and user-reported regressions.
   5.2) If no regressions are observed after 7 days (or 100k tokens served), increase to 25% traffic. Final promotion requires sign-off by Onboarding Lead + Quality Lead.

Metrics, Thresholds & SLOs:
- Production guardrail targets (for routing promotion):
  - Safety failure rate <= 0.1% (blocker if > 0.5%)
  - Hallucination flag rate <= baseline + 1.0 pp
  - Latency P95 <= baseline * 1.15 (blocker if > baseline * 1.3)
  - Token-level cost delta: prefer variants with >= 20% cost savings or clear latency benefits

- Eval metric reporting: every onboarding must publish: baseline metrics table (CSV), per-prompt-set breakdown, human-eval summary, quantization delta table, and CI artifact links.

Prompt sets and Benchmark Management:
- Ownership: Prompt catalog is maintained in `eval-prompt-sets` repo, PR-based updates only.
- Naming convention: `<domain>-<task>-vYYYYMM` (e.g., `emails-classification-v202607`).
- Minimum metadata: domain, task, target-metric, size, source, creation_date, last_review_date.
- Curator checklist for new prompt sets:
  - Confirm representation across demographics and edge cases.
  - Include adversarial subset (10% of examples) flagged for stress testing.
  - Tag known-flaky prompts to exclude from automated baseline comparisons.

Quality Guardrails (checks and remediations):
- Safety: profanity/toxicity checks, PII leak detector, and disallowed content classifier. Remediation: tune prompt, add safety post-filter, or disallow variant.
- Factuality: KB-check recall/precision, semantic similarity to trusted sources. Remediation: add grounding tools, retrieval augmentation, or decrease routing weight.
- Format & Schema checks: JSON/YAML output conformance test. Remediation: use stricter decoding constraints or tool-calling.

Quantization Profiles (standardized):
- profile_fp32: baseline FP32 (reference).
- profile_q8: 8-bit symmetric per-channel quant (fast-path for A100-like inference).
- profile_q4_0: 4-bit static quant (low-cost variant; common fallback).
- profile_int8_ptq: post-training static int8 with calibration set (used for TGI-like runtimes).

Each profile must include: quantization method, calibration dataset reference (prompt_set id), expected latency improvement, and recommended use-cases. Profiles live in `quantization-profiles` directory and require automated validation jobs.

Regression Triage Process (when a regression is detected):
1) Detection sources: CI regression alerts, production monitoring, customer reports, or manual audit.
2) Initial Triage (within 4 hours of alert):
   - Assign incident owner (Applied ML Lead).
   - Capture: affected model variant, prompt-set, delta metrics, and recent deploy/change.
   - If severity = blocker (safety failure or >5% accuracy loss), notify Security + Product and create `regression-incident` ticket.
3) Investigate (24-72 hours):
   - Reproduce against baseline harness and adversarial subsets.
   - Check for dataset drift, tokenization changes, or runtime differences (kernel changes, fused ops).
   - If quantization-related, compare FP32 vs quantized scoring on flagged examples and compute per-example diff traces.
4) Remediation & Rollback:
   - Hotfix options: revert routing policy to baseline model, apply temporary post-filter, or reduce traffic to canary.
   - Long-term fix: retrain/calibrate, adjust prompt templates, or update quantization profile.
5) Postmortem & Preventive Actions (complete within 7 days):
   - Postmortem doc with root cause, timeline, and action owner.
   - Update prompt sets, harness tests, or add new guardrail checks as needed.

CI and Automation Checklist:
- Every onboarding must create CI jobs: `onboard-standard`, `quant-eval`, and `canary-monitor` with thresholds encoded as job checks.
- Evaluation artifacts (CSV, JSONL, charts) must be uploaded to eval DB and linked in the onboarding issue.
- Automated alerts: Slack channel `#applied-ml-regressions` and PagerDuty for severity=blocker.

Operational Playbook Snippets (commands):
- Run baseline harness locally: `rwd-eval run --suite standard-onboarding --model-path /mnt/models/mymodel --out results/baseline.csv`
- Run quant eval: `rwd-eval run --suite quant-eval --model-variants fp32,int8 --prompt-set adversarial --out results/quant.csv`
- Promote canary: `rwd-infra promote --model <id> --variant <v> --traffic 0.05 --notes "onboard canary 2027-07-01"`

Documentation & Reporting:
- Required artifacts to close onboarding: final onboarding issue with artifacts, model card update (model_id and variants table), and a one-page summary for Product/Legal.
- Quarterly reviews: Applied ML provides a quarterly onboarding retrospective summarizing: number of onboards, common failure modes, and updates to prompt sets or quant profiles.

Appendix A - Example metric table (CSV-ready):
- model_id,variant,task,metric,baseline_value,variant_value,delta,latency_p95_baseline,latency_p95_variant,cost_delta
- mdl-123,fp32,qa,exact_match,78.2,78.2,0.0,420ms,420ms,0%
- mdl-123,q4_0,qa,exact_match,78.2,76.4,-1.8,310ms,250ms,-28%

Appendix B - Escalation contacts:
- Applied ML Pager: PD `#applied-ml`
- Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.ai
- SRE lead: sre-lead@redwood.ai

Revision history:
- 2026-06-01: Created (Marina K. Lee)
- 2026-11-15: Added quantization profiles and stricter safety thresholds (reviewers: Diego Ramos)
- 2027-07-01: Updated canary promotion policy and regression SLA (reviewers: Priya Nambiar, Elena Fischer)

Notes and reminders:
- Keep prompt sets small and auditable; prefer multiple narrow prompt sets over one monolithic benchmark.
- All guardrail changes that increase permissiveness require Product + Security review.
- When in doubt, prioritize user safety and fall back to higher-fidelity variants.
